text: You now have two Gold tables built from the same incremental pipeline: gold.daily_sales_summary for Store Operations, and gold.category_breakdown for the Regional Manager. Before you let anyone connect a BI tool to either one, you need to prove something important -- that they actually agree with each other.

Here's why that's even possible to check. Both tables are built from the exact same rows in silver.sales_clean. daily_sales_summary groups those rows by store_id and sale_date, collapsing every category into one number. category_breakdown groups the same rows by store_id, category, and sale_date -- one level more detailed. Same source, different grain, which means there's a guaranteed relationship between them.

If you take category_breakdown and sum total_sales back up across every category, for a given store and day, you must land on exactly the same number as daily_sales_summary for that same store and day. This query does exactly that: it rolls category_breakdown up to the store-and-day grain, joins it against daily_sales_summary, and flags any row where the two numbers differ by more than one cent.

Here's the same logic as a PySpark DataFrame job, if you'd rather run it from a notebook cell instead of a SQL editor. Group category_breakdown by store_id and sale_date, sum total_sales, join against daily_sales_summary, and filter down to rows where the absolute difference exceeds that one-cent tolerance. The result either way is a discrepancy report -- the actual rows that are wrong, not just a pass-or-fail flag.

That one-cent tolerance matters. It exists only to absorb tiny floating-point rounding noise from summing currency at different grouping levels -- it is not there to hide real problems. Run this query right now, against the pipeline as it stands after Lessons 7 and 8, and it should return zero rows. Both Gold tables were built correctly from the same Silver data, so everything reconciles.

Save this query somewhere you'll actually find it again. It is clean today, but it becomes the exact diagnostic tool you reach for later in this course, when something in this pipeline really does break and you need to prove, and then find, precisely where the numbers stopped agreeing. Next lesson, you'll connect Power BI to both of these Gold tables for the first time.
